value.author: pi-glm
value.text: Review round (PR #8, CodeRabbit thread on the declaration admission flow): verified the finding. An over-limit declaration (operands plus evidence merging to more than sixteen distinct source fragments) was admitted durably and only failed at derivation, after consuming a declaration slot, a replay slot and the version-2 upgrade. Fix: declaration admission now previews the authorized addition through the same exported evaluator the derive path uses, so limit_exceeded refuses before any durable side effect; no second copy of capacity or precision logic exists. A same-class self-review found the preview also catches exact-precision and interval-corner overflow at admission, which a literal sixteen-fragment guard alone would have missed.

value.author: pi-glm
value.text: Revert proof for the review fix: node test/revert.acceptance.ts --partitions-only reports 11/11 expected behavioral failures, including the new declaration-admission-preview entry whose removal fails the capacity and precision admission regressions, followed by a passing unchanged implementation. New regression tests: partition admission refuses exact operands whose reviewed sum cannot persist (sixteen-fragment and eighty-digit precision cases refuse before any write, native history unchanged), plus a post-admission over-capacity declaration refusal in the refusals suite.
